Has anyone else here actually taken the Harvard Implicit Association Test they're basing this data on? Anyone can go online and take it, as many times as they want, so I don't trust this data to be particularly accurate in the first place.
The test gives you a list of positive and negative words and asks you to sort them positive words on one side and negative words on the other. They also mix in pictures of white and black faces, (grayscale pictures so you can't just go off color) and have you sort white to the same side as positive, and black to the negative side. So you have words and pictures of faces popping up at you, and you are asked to sort them as fast as possible because being slower with one type of face means you're racist trying to cover for it.
Then when you're just getting used to sending white faces to the right with positive words and black faces with negative words to the left, they switch it up, and have you sort positive words to the same side as the black faces, and the white faces with the negative words. Accidentally sending the faces to the sides you just got used to associating them with, now counts toward your racism. And hesitation because you're having to break a newly-formed habit, also skews your score toward more racist.

It's basically designed to trick you into picking answers that make you look racist, even if you were from another planet and had no idea about human racial stereotypes. That data isn't reliable at all. Any conclusions drawn from it are unlikely to have any bearing on the real world.
